core_obligations: Reduce the definition to a finite purely inseparable extension k' of k (proof line 47427).

Write k' as obtained from k by adjoining finitely many variables subject to finitely many relations, and move that finite data into a single step k_i of the colimit, producing a finite purely inseparable extension k_i' of k_i (proof lines 47428-47431).
Identify the base change A tensor over k with k' with A tensor over k_i with k_i' and apply the hypothesis that A is geometrically regular over k_i (proof lines 47431-47432).
proof_roadmap: Turn a finite purely inseparable extension of the colimit into one of a single subfield (proof lines 47426-47431).
Match the two base changes and apply the hypothesis at that step (proof lines 47431-47433).
difficulty_reason: If a field k is a directed colimit of subfields k_i and an algebra A is geometrically regular over each k_i, the lemma concludes that A is geometrically regular over k (statement lines 47418-47424). The proof does not work with the definition directly over all field extensions: it reduces to a finite purely inseparable extension k', observes that such an extension is described by finitely many generators and relations and therefore occurs already over some k_i, and then identifies the two base changes (proof lines 47426-47433). Moving finite data down the directed colimit is the step that carries the content, and the author writes it out; the text is copied verbatim including its wording about the two extensions. H2.
